children.text: Chapter 1
yatho etaddhutaḥ prahuta āhutaḥ śūlagavo baliharaṇaṃ pratyavarohaṇam aṣṭakāhoma iti sapta pākayajñasaṃsthā iti ||
children.translated_text: As follows: huta, prahuta, āhuta, śūlagava, baliharaṇa, pratyavarohaṇa, and aṣṭakāhoma: these are the seven institutions of <s>pākayajña</s> (cooked domestic sacrifice).

children.text: tā anuvyākhyāsyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: We shall explain them in detail.

children.text: tatra yaddhūyate sa huto yathaitad vivāhaḥ sīmantonnayanaṃ ceti ||
children.translated_text: Among these, what is offered in the fire is huta, as for example marriage and <s>sīmantonnayana</s> (parting of the pregnant woman's hair).

children.text: tatra hi hūyata eva ||
children.translated_text: For in that case it is simply offered in the fire.

children.text: atha yaddhutvā dīyate sa prahuto yathaitaj jātakarma caulaṃ ceti ||
children.translated_text: Next, what is given after being offered in the fire is prahuta, as for example the birth rite and the tonsure rite.

children.text: tatra hi hutvā dīyata eva ||
children.translated_text: For in that case it is given only after having been offered in the fire.

children.text: atha yaddhutvā dattvā cādīyate sa āhutaḥ yathaitad upanayanaṃ samāvartanaṃ ceti ||
children.translated_text: Next, what is taken after being offered in the fire and given is āhuta, as for example initiation and the return from studentship.

children.text: tatra hi hutvā dattvā cādīyate ||
children.translated_text: For in that case it is taken only after having been offered in the fire and given.

children.text: atha yacchūleṣūpanīya gavyāni śrapayanti sa śūlagavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Next, when they bring up cattle-products on spits and cook them, that is śūlagava.

children.text: atha yat gṛhyābhyo devatābhyo 'nnaṃ saṃprakiranti tat baliharaṇam ||
children.translated_text: Next, when they scatter food for the domestic deities, that is baliharaṇa.

children.text: atha yad ṛto ṛtuṃ pratyavarohanti tat pratyavarohaṇam ||
children.translated_text: Next, when they descend again season after season, that is pratyavarohaṇa.

children.text: atha yad ekāṣṭakāyām annaṃ kriyate so 'ṣṭakāhoma iti ||
children.translated_text: Next, when food is prepared on the <s>Ekāṣṭakā</s>, that is called aṣṭakāhoma.

children.text: vivāhaṃ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: We shall explain marriage.

children.text: udagayana āpūryamāṇapakṣe puṇye nakṣatre yugmān brāhmaṇān varān prahiṇoti prasugmantā dhiyasānasya sakṣaṇi varebhir varān abhiṣuprasīdata
children.translated_text: During the sun's northward course, in the waxing fortnight, under an auspicious constellation, he sends forth an even number of Brahmins as wooers, saying: 'May you, setting out prosperously with the thought of the thoughtful one, graciously approach the wooers with wooers.'

children.text: asmākam indra ubhayaṃ jujoṣati yat saumyasyāndhaso bubodhati iti ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Indra</s> favors both things of ours, when he becomes aware of the Soma-draught.'

children.text: yato 'numantrayate anṛkṣarā ṛjavas santu panthā yebhis sakhāyo yanti no vareyam
children.translated_text: From where he gives consent, he says: 'May the paths by which our companions go to woo be free from danger and straight.'

children.text: sam aryamā sam bhago no ninīyāt sañjāspatyaṃ suyamam astu devāḥ iti ||
children.translated_text: 'May <s>Aryaman</s> and <s>Bhaga</s> lead us together; may the gods grant well-restrained household union.'

children.text: atha yadi dakṣiṇābhis saha dattā syān nātra varān prahiṇuyāt ||
children.translated_text: But if she has been given together with gifts, he should not send wooers in this case.

children.text: tāṃ pratigṛhṇīyāt prajāpatistriyāṃ yaśaḥ ity etābhiṣ ṣaḍbhir anucchandasam ||
children.translated_text: He should receive her with these six verses, beginning 'In a woman <s>Prajāpati</s> placed fame,' without regard to metre.

children.text: sarve māsā vivāhasya ||
children.translated_text: All months are suitable for marriage.

children.text: śucitapastapasyavarjam ity eke ||
children.translated_text: Some say, 'except <s>Śuci</s>, <s>Tapas</s>, and <s>Tapasya</s>.'

children.text: rohiṇī mṛgaśīrṣam uttare phalgunī svātīti vivāhasya nakṣatrāṇi ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rohiṇī</s>, <s>Mṛgaśīrṣa</s>, <s>Uttara Phalgunī</s>, and <s>Svātī</s> are the constellations for marriage.

children.text: punarvasū tiṣyo hastaś śroṇā revatīty anyeṣāṃ bhūtikarmaṇām ||
children.translated_text: <s>Punarvasu</s>, <s>Tiṣya</s>, <s>Hasta</s>, <s>Śroṇā</s>, and <s>Revatī</s> are for other rites intended for prosperity.

children.text: yāni cānyāni puṇyoktāni nakṣatrāṇi teṣu pūrvedyur evarddhipūrteṣu yugmān brāhmaṇān bhojayet ||
children.translated_text: And under whatever other constellations are said to be auspicious, on the preceding day, when the prosperity rite has been completed, he should feed an even number of Brahmins.

children.text: pradakṣiṇam upacāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: The procedure is clockwise.

children.text: puṣpaphalākṣatamiśrair yavais tilārtham upaliṣyāṃ dadhy odanaṃ samprakīrya dakṣiṇaṃ jānuṃ bhūmau nidhāya savyam uddhṛtya iḍā devahūḥ iti japitvā nāndīmukhāḥ pitaraḥ priyantām iti vācayitvā adya vivāhaḥ iti brāhmaṇān annena pariviṣya puṇyāhaṃ svasti ṛddhim ity oṅkārapūrvaṃ tristrir ekaikām āśiṣo vācayitvā snāto 'hatavāso gandhānuliptas sragvī bhuktavān pratodapāṇir apadātir gatvā vadhūjñātibhir atithivad arcitas snātām ahatavāsasāṃ gandhānuliptāṃ sragviṇīṃ bhuktavatīm iṣuhastāṃ dattāṃ vadhūṃ samīkṣate abhrātṛghnīṃ varuṇāpatighnīṃ bṛhaspate indrāputraghnīṃ lakṣmyaṃ tām asyai savitas suva iti ||
children.translated_text: Having smeared barley mixed with flowers, fruits, and unbroken grains in place of sesame, scattered curds and rice, placed his right knee on the ground and raised the left, recited 'Iḍā is invoked by the gods,' had it proclaimed 'May the ancestors with Nandī at their head be pleased,' and, saying 'Today is the marriage,' served the Brahmins with food, he has each blessing, 'auspicious day, welfare, prosperity,' pronounced three times each, preceded by oṃ. Then, bathed, wearing unworn clothes, anointed with perfumes, garlanded, having eaten, holding a goad in his hand and not going on foot, he goes; honored like a guest by the bride's kinsmen, he looks upon the bride, who has bathed, is dressed in unworn garments, anointed with perfumes, garlanded, has eaten, holds an arrow in her hand, and has been given, saying: 'Not killing a brother, not killing a husband through <s>Varuṇa</s>, not killing a son through <s>Bṛhaspati</s> and <s>Indra</s>, possessed of fortune: may <s>Savitṛ</s> impel her for this woman.'

children.text: tayekṣyamāṇo japati aghoracakṣur apatighny edhi śivā patibhyas sumanās suvarcāḥ
children.translated_text: While being looked at by her, he recites: 'Be one whose eye is not terrible, not destructive to your husband, auspicious for your husbands, kindly disposed and bright.'

children.text: jīvasūr devakāmā syonā śaṃ no bhava dvipade śaṃ catuṣpade iti ||
children.translated_text: 'Mother of living sons, devoted to the gods, gracious, be welfare for our bipeds and welfare for our quadrupeds.'

children.text: athainām antareṇa bhrumukhe darbheṇa saṃmārṣṭi idam ahaṃ yā tvayi patighny alakṣmis tāṃ nirdiśāmi iti ||
children.translated_text: Then he wipes her between the brows and the face with darbha grass, saying: 'This misfortune in you that destroys a husband, I point it away.'

children.text: darbhaṃ nirasyāpa upaspṛśyāthaināṃ dakṣiṇe haste gṛhṇāti mitro 'si iti ||
children.translated_text: Having thrown away the darbha grass and touched water, he then takes her by the right hand, saying: 'You are <s>Mitra</s>.'

children.text: athaināṃ devayajanam udānayati ekam iṣe viṣṇus tvā 'nvetu
children.translated_text: Then he leads her up to the sacrificial place: 'One step for nourishment; may <s>Viṣṇu</s> follow you.'

children.text: dve ūrje viṣṇus tvā 'nvetu
children.translated_text: 'Two steps for strength; may <s>Viṣṇu</s> follow you.'

children.text: trīṇi vratāya viṣṇus tvā 'nvetu
children.translated_text: 'Three steps for the vow; may <s>Viṣṇu</s> follow you.'

children.text: catvāri māyobhavāya viṣṇus tvā 'nvetu
children.translated_text: 'Four steps for well-being; may <s>Viṣṇu</s> follow you.'

children.text: pañca paśubhyo viṣṇus tvā 'nvetu
children.translated_text: 'Five steps for cattle; may <s>Viṣṇu</s> follow you.'

children.text: ṣaḍ āyaspoṃṣāya viṣṇus tvā 'nvetu
children.translated_text: 'Six steps for flourishing vigor; may <s>Viṣṇu</s> follow you.'

children.text: saptabhyo hotrābhyo viṣṇus tvā 'nvetu iti ||
children.translated_text: 'For the seven priestly offices; may <s>Viṣṇu</s> follow you.'

children.text: saptamaṃ padam upasaṃgṛhya japati sakhāyas saptapadā abhūma sakhyaṃ te gameyaṃ sakhyāt te mā yoṣaṃ sakhyān me mā yoṣṭhāḥ iti ||
children.translated_text: Having taken hold at the seventh step, he recites: 'We have become companions by the seven steps. May I attain your companionship; may I not be separated from your companionship; may you not be separated from my companionship.'

children.text: Chapter 2
āvedyārghyaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: After announcing it, he should perform the arghya offering.

children.text: madhye 'gārasyodīcīnapratiṣevaṇā erakā upastṛṇāti ||
children.translated_text: In the middle of the house he spreads eraka grass with its tips turned northward.

children.text: tāsv ahatāni bahuguṇāny uttaradaśāni vāsāṃsy āstīrya teṣvṛtvijaḥ prāṅmukhā upaviśanti ||
children.translated_text: On these he spreads unworn garments of many folds, with their fringes to the north, and on them the officiants sit facing east.

children.text: uttarapūrve deśe 'gārasya prākkūlān darbhān saṃstīrya teṣv arghyadravyāṇi saṃsādayati ||
children.translated_text: In the northeastern part of the house he spreads darbha grass with its tips to the east and arranges the arghya materials on it.

children.text: yāvanta ṛtvijas tāvanti kāṃsyāni pātrāṇi sāpidhānāni tāvataḥ kūrcān ||
children.translated_text: There should be as many bronze vessels with lids as there are officiants, and the same number of seats of darbha grass.

children.text: dvāvanyau parigrahaṇīyau kūrcau ||
children.translated_text: Two other darbha seats are to be taken in addition.

children.text: dadhi madhu ghṛtam āpaḥ payo vastrayugāni kuṇḍalayugāni ||
children.translated_text: Curds, honey, ghee, water, milk, pairs of garments, and pairs of earrings are set out.

children.text: yasyai goḥ payaś camasaḥ srag alaṃkaraṇīyaṃ ceti ||
children.translated_text: Also a ladle from the cow whose milk is used, a garland, and what is needed for adornment.

children.text: pavitre kṛtvā tūṣṇīṃ saṃskṛtābhir adbhir uttānāni pātrāṇi kṛtvā prokṣya kūrce kāṃsyaṃ nidhāya tiraḥpavitraṃ madhvānayati ||
children.translated_text: Having made the purifiers, silently made the vessels face upward, sprinkled them with consecrated waters, placed the bronze vessel on a darbha seat, he brings the honey through the purifier.

children.text: dadhi payo vā dvitīyaṃ sa dvivṛt ||
children.translated_text: Curds or milk is the second; that makes it twofold.

children.text: ghṛtaṃ tṛtīyaṃ sa trivṛt ||
children.translated_text: Ghee is the third; that makes it threefold.

children.text: yad dvitīyaṃ taccaturthaṃ sa caturvṛt ||
children.translated_text: Whatever is second is also the fourth; that makes it fourfold.

children.text: āpaḥ pañcamīḥ sa pāṅktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The waters are the fifth; together with it he is fivefold.

children.text: varṣīyasā tejomayenāpidhāya nānāpuruṣā arghyadravyāṇyādadate anvag anusaṃvrajatā ||
children.translated_text: Having covered it with a larger, radiant covering, different men take up the arghya materials, proceeding along behind him one after another.

children.text: kūrcaḥ iti kūrcaṃ prāha ||
children.translated_text: He says, 'The darbha-seat,' referring to the darbha-seat.

children.text: tat sukūrcaḥ itītaraḥ pratigṛhṇāti ||
children.translated_text: The other receives it, saying, 'That is a good darbha-seat.'

children.text: taṃ pradakṣiṇaṃ paryasyodagāvṛtta upaviśati ||
children.translated_text: Having carried it around clockwise, he sits down turned toward the north.

children.text: purastād vaṃna pratyañcam upohate rāṣṭrabhṛd asyācāryāsandī mā tvad yoṣam iti ||
children.translated_text: In front he brings it near, facing west, saying, 'It is the support of the realm; this is the teacher's seat; may I not be separated from you.'

children.text: athāsmā udapātram ādāya kūrcābhyāṃ parigṛhya pādyā āpa iti prāha ||
children.translated_text: Then, taking a water vessel for him and enclosing it with the two darbha bunches, he says, 'Water for washing the feet.'

children.text: tā abhimantrayate āpaḥ pādāv anejānīr dviṣantaṃ nāśayantu me
children.translated_text: He addresses those waters with the mantra: 'Waters, washing the feet, may you destroy the one who hates me;

children.text: asmin kule brahmavarcasy asāni iti ||
children.translated_text: may I be endowed with brahmanic radiance in this family.'

children.text: dakṣiṇaṃ pādaṃ pūrvaṃ brāhmaṇāya prasārayati
children.translated_text: For a Brahmin he extends the right foot first;

children.text: svayaṃ śūdrāya ||
children.translated_text: for a Śūdra, he does so himself.

children.text: strī prakṣālayati pumān abhiṣiñcati
children.translated_text: A woman washes it and a man pours water over it;

children.text: viparītam ity eke ||
children.translated_text: some say the reverse.

children.text: niyamāt patnīyajamānau jaṅghre dhāvayataḥ ||
children.translated_text: According to rule, the wife and the sacrificer wash the shanks.

children.text: avanektuḥ pāṇī saṃmṛśati mayi maho mayi bhago mayi bhargo mayi yaśaḥ iti ||
children.translated_text: He touches the hands of the washer, saying, 'In me be greatness; in me fortune; in me splendor; in me fame.'

children.text: athāpa upaspṛśya mayīndriyaṃ vīryam ity uraḥpratyātmānaṃ pratyabhimṛśate ||
children.translated_text: Then, having sipped water, he touches himself on the chest, saying, 'In me be power and vigor.'

children.text: apo vrīhibhir yavair vā samudāyutya tathaiva kūrcābhyāṃ parigṛhyārhaṇīyā āpa iti prāha ||
children.translated_text: Having mixed water with rice-grains or barley-grains and, in the same way, enclosed it with the two darbha bunches, he says, 'Water worthy of honor.'

children.text: tā abhimantraye āma āgād varcasā yaśamā saṃsṛja payasā tejasā ca
children.translated_text: He addresses it: 'The raw draught has come; unite me with radiance and fame, with milk and brilliance;

children.text: taṃ mā priyaṃ prajānāṃ kurv adhipatiṃ paśūnām iti ||
children.translated_text: make me beloved among creatures, lord over cattle.'

children.text: ekadeśam añjalābānīyamānam anumantraye virājo 'si virājo doham aśīya
children.translated_text: As a portion is being brought in the joined hands, he assents with the mantra: 'You are virāj; may I obtain the milking of virāj;

children.text: mama padyāya virāja iti ||
children.translated_text: for my step, through virāj.'

children.text: atiśiṣṭāḥ parācīrninīyamānā anumantraye samudraṃ vaḥ prahiṇomyakṣitāḥ svā yonim api gacchata
children.translated_text: As what remains is being carried away toward the west, he assents: 'I send you, undecaying, to the ocean; go back to your own womb.

children.text: acchidraḥ prajayā bhūyāsaṃ mā parāsoci matpayaḥ iti ||
children.translated_text: May I be unbroken in offspring; may my milk not be lost away from me.'

children.text: atha tathaiva kūrcābhyāṃ parigṛhyopastaraṇīyā āpa iti prāha ||
children.translated_text: Then, enclosing it in the same way with the two darbha bunches, he says, 'Water for laying beneath.'

children.text: tā pibati amṛtopastaraṇam asi iti ||
children.translated_text: He drinks it, saying, 'You are the underlay of immortality.'

children.text: trir ācamet triḥ parimṛjet
children.translated_text: He should sip three times and wipe three times;

children.text: dvir ity eke ||
children.translated_text: some say twice.

children.text: ācāntāyāpāvṛttāya tathaiva kūrcābhyāṃ parigṛhyārghya iti prāha madhuparka iti vā ||
children.translated_text: For him who has sipped and turned back, enclosing it in the same way with the two darbha bunches, he says, 'Arghya,' or else, 'Madhuparka.'

children.text: madhuparkaṃ proktam anumantrayate trayyai vidyāyai yaśo 'si yaśaso yaśo 'si brahmaṇo dīptir asi
children.translated_text: When the madhuparka has been announced, he assents: 'You are fame for the threefold knowledge; you are the fame of fame; you are the brilliance of brahman;

children.text: taṃ mā priyaṃ prajānāṃ kurvadhipatiṃ paśūnām iti ||
children.translated_text: make me beloved among creatures, lord over cattle.'

children.text: tam ubhābhyāṃ hastābhyāṃ pratigṛhṇāti devasya tvā savituḥ prasave 'śvinor bāhubhyāṃ pūṣṇo hastābhyāṃ pratigṛhṇāmi iti ||
children.translated_text: He receives it with both hands, saying, 'At the impulse of the god <s>Savitṛ</s>, with the arms of the <s>Aśvins</s>, with the hands of <s>Pūṣan</s>, I receive you.'

children.text: tasmiṃś cit kiṃcid āpatitaṃ syāt tad aṅguṣṭhena ca mahānāmvyā copasaṃgṛhyemāṃ diśaṃ nirasyati neṣṭāv ṛddhiṃ kṛntāmi yā te ghorā tanūḥ
children.translated_text: If anything whatever has fallen into it, taking that up with the thumb and the ring finger, he throws it away in this direction, saying, 'I do not cut off prosperity from the desired object; that terrible body of yours,

children.text: tayā tam āviśa yo 'smān dveṣṭi yaṃ ca vayaṃ dviṣmaḥ iti ||
children.translated_text: with it enter the one who hates us and whom we hate.'

children.text: athāpa upaspṛśya sarvābhir aṅgulībhiḥ samudāyutya prāśnāti yan madhuno madhavyaṃ paramamannādyaṃ vīryam
children.translated_text: Then, having sipped water and stirred it with all his fingers, he eats, saying, 'What honeyed thing belongs to honey, the highest strength of food,

children.text: tenāha madhuno madhavyena parameṇānnādyena vīryeṇa paramo 'nnādo madhavyo 'sāni iti ||
children.translated_text: with that honeyed thing of honey, with the highest food-strength, may I become the highest eater of food, honeyed.'

children.text: triḥ prāśya trir anupibeccheṣaṃ ca kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: Having eaten three times, he should drink after it three times and leave a remainder.

children.text: ya ātmanaḥ śreyāṃsam icchet tasmai śeṣaṃ dadyād iti ||
children.translated_text: He should give the remainder to one for whom he desires superiority over himself.

children.text: ācāntāyāpāvṛttāya tathaiva kūrcābhyāṃ parigṛhyāpidhānīyā āpa iti prāha ||
children.translated_text: For him who has sipped and turned back, enclosing it in the same way with the two darbha bunches, he says, 'Water for covering.'

children.text: tāḥ pibati amṛtāpidhānam asi iti ||
children.translated_text: He drinks it, saying, 'You are the covering of immortality.'

children.text: trir ācāmet triḥ parimṛjet
children.translated_text: He should sip three times and wipe three times;

children.text: dvir ity eke ||
children.translated_text: some say twice.

children.text: ācāntāyāpāvṛttāya gaur iti gāṃ prāha ||
children.translated_text: For him who has sipped and turned back, he says, 'The cow,' referring to the cow.

children.text: tām anumantrayate gaur asyapahatapāpmāpa pāpmānaṃ nuda mama cāmuṣya ca ity upavettur nāma gṛhṇāti ||
children.translated_text: He assents to her: 'You are a cow, remover of evil; drive away evil from me and from this man,' naming the attendant.

children.text: nānā mahartvigbhyo gāḥ prāha ||
children.translated_text: He announces separate cows for the great officiants.

children.text: ekāṃ hotṛkebhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: One cow is for the Hotṛ priests.

children.text: sarvebhyo vaikām avibhavatvāt ||
children.translated_text: Or one cow is for all, because of insufficiency.

children.text: yaḥ prāha tasmā upākaroty ekadeśaṃ vapāya juhoti agniḥ prathamaḥ prāśnātu sa hi veda yathā haviḥ
children.translated_text: For the one who announces it, he brings it near; he offers a portion as omentum, saying, '<s>Agni</s> shall eat first, for he knows how the oblation is;

children.text: śivā asmābhyamopadhīḥ kṛṇotu viśvacarṣaṇiḥ iti ||
children.translated_text: may the all-seeing one make the medicines auspicious for us.'

children.text: ekadeśam upaharati tat prāśnāti agniḥ prathamaḥ prāśnātu sa hi veda yathā haviḥ
children.translated_text: He brings forward a portion; that he eats, saying, '<s>Agni</s> shall eat first, for he knows how the oblation is;

children.text: ariṣṭam asmākaṃ kṛṇotv asau brāhmaṇo brāhmaṇeṣu iti
children.translated_text: may that Brahmin make safety for us among Brahmins.'

children.text: atha yad utsrakṣyan bhavati tām anumantrayate gaur dhenubhavyā mātā rudrāṇāṃ duhitā vasūnāṃ svasādityānām amṛtasya nābhiḥ
children.translated_text: Then, when he is about to release her, he assents to her: 'The cow, destined to become a milch-cow, mother of the <s>Rudras</s>, daughter of the <s>Vasus</s>, sister of the <s>Ādityas</s>, navel of immortality:

children.text: pra ṇu vocaṃ cikituṣe janāya mā gām anāgām aditiṃ vadhiṣṭa
children.translated_text: I proclaim to the discerning person: do not kill the guiltless cow, <s>Aditi</s>.'

children.text: pibatūdakaṃ tṛṇānyatta
children.translated_text: 'Let her drink water; let her eat grasses.'

children.text: om utsṛjata iti ||
children.translated_text: 'Oṃ, release her,' he says.

children.text: tasyām utsṛṣṭāyāṃ meṣamajaṃ vālabhate ||
children.translated_text: When she has been released, he takes hold of a ram or a goat.

children.text: āraṇyena vā māṃsena ||
children.translated_text: Or he uses meat from a wild animal.

children.text: na tvevāmāṃso 'rghyaḥ syāt ||
children.translated_text: But the arghya must never be without meat.

children.text: aśaktau piṣṭānnaṃ saṃsidhyet ||
children.translated_text: If he is unable, a prepared flour-cake should be made ready.

children.text: siddhe bhūtam iti prāha ||
children.translated_text: When it is prepared, he says, 'It has become.'

children.text: tat subhūtam iti itaraḥ pratyāha ||
children.translated_text: The other replies, 'It has become well.'

children.text: tad abhimantrayate bhūtaṃ subhūtaṃ sā virāṭ tan mā kṣāyi tan me 'śīya tan ma ūrjaṃ vā oṃ kalpayata iti ||
children.translated_text: He addresses it: 'Become, well become; that is virāj. May that not fail me; may I eat that; prepare that for my nourishment, indeed, oṃ.'

children.text: caturo nānāgotrān brāhmaṇān bhojayatety eva brūyāt ||
children.translated_text: He should simply say, 'Feed four Brahmins of different gotras.'

children.text: teṣu bhuktavatsvannamasmā upaharati ||
children.translated_text: When they have eaten, he brings food to him.

children.text: tat prāśnāti virāḍasi virāḍannaṃ virāḍrivārājo mayi dhehi iti ||
children.translated_text: He eats it, saying, 'You are virāj; food is virāj; place in me the sovereignty of virāj.'

children.text: bhuktavadbhyo vastrayugāni kuṇḍalayugāni yasyai goḥ payaś camasaḥ srag alaṃkaraṇīyam iti ca dadyāt
children.translated_text: To those who have eaten he should give pairs of garments, pairs of earrings, the milk of the cow, the ladle, a garland, and whatever is needed for adornment.

children.text: ekadhanaṃ ṣaṣṭhauhīṃ damyāv ity eke ||
children.translated_text: Some say: one single fee, a cow in her sixth year, and a pair of tamed animals.

children.text: prāṅmadhuparkād alaṃkaraṇam eke samāmananti ||
children.translated_text: Some recite the adornment as taking place before the <s>madhuparka</s>.

children.text: mahayed ṛtvijam ācārya cātmānaṃ vā eṣa mahayati yaḥ samṛtvijam ācāryaṃ ca mahayaty evam evaṃvratā vā ātyantikāḥ syuḥ patito 'nanūcāna iti nimittāni ||
children.translated_text: He should honor the officiating priest and the teacher. For he truly honors himself who honors the officiating priest and the teacher together. Thus, in this same way, those who keep such a vow should be honored for life. The marks of exclusion are: one who has fallen, or one who has not studied.

children.text: varaṇe 'gnyādheyaprabhṛtiṣu caiṣāmṛtvijaṃ smaret ||
children.translated_text: At the choosing of priests, and in rites beginning with the establishment of the sacred fires, one should remember their officiating priest.

children.text: tathaite arghyā ṛtvik śvaśuraḥ pitṛvyo mātula ācāryo rājā vā snātakaḥ priyo varo 'tithir iti ||
children.translated_text: Likewise these are recipients of the arghya: an officiating priest, a father-in-law, a paternal uncle, a maternal uncle, a teacher, a king, a snātaka, a dear friend, a bridegroom, and a guest.

children.text: saṃvatsaraparyāgatebhya etebhya evaṃ kuryāt vivāhe varāya ||
children.translated_text: When these same persons return after a year, he should do this for them; at a wedding, for the bridegroom.

children.text: athartvigbhyaḥ karmaṇi karmaṇi dadāti ||
children.translated_text: Then he gives to the officiating priests at each separate rite.

children.text: Chapter 3
atha śucau same deśe agnyāyatanadeśaṃ śakalena triḥ prācīnam ullikhet trir udīcīnam ||
children.translated_text: Then, in a pure and level place, he should mark out the site for the fire-place with a splinter, three times toward the east and three times toward the north.

children.text: athādbhir abhyukṣya śakalaṃ nirasyāpa upaspṛśya yājñikāt kāṣṭhād agniṃ mathitvā śrotriyāgārād vāhṛtya vyāhṛtibhir nirupyopasamādhāyopatiṣṭhate ||
children.translated_text: Then, having sprinkled it with water, thrown away the splinter, touched water, kindled the fire from sacrificial wood by churning, or brought it from the house of a learned Brahmin, he sets it down with the vyāhṛtis, lays it properly, and attends upon it.

children.text: juṣṭo damūnā atithidurgeṇa imaṃ no yajñam upayā hi vidrān
children.translated_text: 'Well-pleased, dwelling in the house, with hospitality as protection, come knowingly to this sacrifice of ours,

children.text: viśvā agne 'bhiyujo vihatya śatrūyatāmābharā bhojanāni iti ||
children.translated_text: having struck down all attackers, O <s>Agni</s>; bring us the foods of those who act as enemies.' Thus.

children.text: athainaṃ pradakṣiṇamagniṃ parisamūhya paryṛkṣya paristīrya prāgagrairdarbhair agniṃ paristṛṇāti ||
children.translated_text: Then, having swept around this fire clockwise, sprinkled around it, and strewn around it, he surrounds the fire with darbha grasses whose tips point east.

children.text: api vodagagrāḥ paścāc ca purastāc ca bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: Or they may have their tips pointing north, both behind and in front.

children.text: dakṣiṇān uttarān uttarān adharān yadi prāgudagagrāḥ ||
children.translated_text: If the tips point northeast, the southern ones are placed above the northern, and the northern above the lower ones.

children.text: uttareṇāgniṃ prāgagrān darbhān saṃstīrya teṣu dvandvaṃ nyacci pātrāṇi saṃsādayati devasaṃyuktāny ekaikaśaḥ pitṛsaṃyuktāni sakṛd eva manuṣyasaṃyuktāni ||
children.translated_text: North of the fire he spreads darbha grasses with tips to the east, and on them he sets down the vessels in pairs, upside down: those connected with the gods one by one, those connected with the ancestors all at once, and those connected with humans all together.

children.text: yat saha sarvāṇi mānuṣāṇi ity etasmād brāhmaṇāt ||
children.translated_text: This is on the authority of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> statement: 'All human vessels are together.'

children.text: pavitre kṛtvā tūṣṇīṃ saṃskṛtābhir adbhir uttānāni pātrāṇi kṛtvā prokṣya vistrasyedhmaṃ tris sarvābhiḥ prokṣati ||
children.translated_text: Having made the purifiers, silently turned the vessels upward and sprinkled them with consecrated waters, he should scatter the fuel-sticks and sprinkle them three times with all the waters.

children.text: darbheṣu dakṣiṇato brāhmaṇa upaviśati utarata udapātram ||
children.translated_text: A Brahmin sits on the darbha grasses to the south; the water-vessel is to the north.

children.text: atha tiraḥpavitramājyasthālyām ājyaṃ nirupyodīco 'ṅgārānnirūhya yantān kṛtvā teṣv adhiśrityābhidyotanenābhidyotya dve darbhāgre pracchidya prakṣālya pratyasya punar abhidyotya triḥ paryagnikṛtvā vartma kurvann udagudvāsya pratyūhyāṅgārān barhir āstīrya athainad udīcīnāgrābhyāṃ pavitrābhyāṃ punar āhāraṃ trir utpūya vistrasya pavitre 'dbhiḥ saṃspṛśyāgnāv anupraharati ||
children.translated_text: Then, through the purifier, he pours the ghee into the ghee-pot, draws embers out to the north, makes supports, sets it upon them, illuminates it with a firebrand, cuts off two tips of darbha grass, washes them, throws them back, illuminates it again, carries it round the fire three times, making a path, lifts it off toward the north, pushes the embers back, spreads the sacrificial grass, and then, with two purifiers whose tips point north, purifies this again three times by bringing it back, scatters it, touches the purifiers with water, and throws them after into the fire.

children.text: atha darvī niṣṭapya darbhaiḥ saṃmṛjyādbhiḥ saṃspṛśya punar niṣṭapya prokṣya nidhāya darbhān adbhiḥ saṃspṛśyāgnāv anupraharati ||
children.translated_text: Then, having heated the ladle, wiped it with darbha grass, touched it with water, heated it again, sprinkled it, and set it down, he touches the darbha grasses with water and throws them after into the fire.

children.text: atha śamyāḥ paridhāti svādirī darvī tejaskāmasyaudumbaryannādyakāmasya pālāśī brahmavarcasakāmasya iti ||
children.translated_text: Then he places the enclosing sticks. The ladle is of svādirī wood for one desiring brilliance, of udumbara wood for one desiring food, and of palāśa wood for one desiring sacred learning.

children.text: atha haikeṣāṃ vijñāyate nirṛtigṛhitā vai darvīṃ yad darvyā juhuyān nirṛtyā 'sya yajñaṃ grāhayet tasmāt sruveṇaiva hotavyam iti ||
children.translated_text: Now among some the following is known: 'The ladle is seized by <s>Nirṛti</s>; if one were to offer with the ladle, he would cause his sacrifice to be seized by <s>Nirṛti</s>. Therefore one should offer only with the sruva.'

children.text: pālāśena sruveṇety ātreyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'With a sruva of palāśa wood,' says <s>Ātreya</s>.

children.text: khādireṇety āṅgirasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'With one of khadira wood,' says <s>Āṅgirasa</s>.

children.text: tāmrāyasenety ātharvaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'With one of copper,' says <s>Ātharvaṇa</s>.

children.text: kārṣṇāyasenābhicarann iti sārvatrikam ||
children.translated_text: 'With one of black iron when performing hostile rites': this is the general rule.

children.text: anyo vā 'syaitāvatkṛtvāgamanaṃ kāṅkṣet ||
children.translated_text: Or someone else, having done this much for him, may wait for his arrival.

children.text: apareṇāgnim udīcīnapratiṣevaṇām erakāṃ sādhivāsām āstīrya tasyāṃ prāñcāv upaviśata uttarataḥ patir dakṣiṇā patnī ||
children.translated_text: West of the fire he spreads eraka grass with a covering, its edging toward the north; on it the two sit facing east, the husband to the north and the wife to the south.

children.text: athānvārabdhāyāṃ pradakṣiṇam agniṃ pariṣiñcati ||
children.translated_text: Then, while she has taken hold of him, he sprinkles water around the fire clockwise.

children.text: adite 'numanyasva iti dakṣiṇataḥ prācīnam ||
children.translated_text: With 'O <s>Aditi</s>, give permission,' he sprinkles from the south toward the east.

children.text: anumate 'numanyasva iti paścād udīcīnam ||
children.translated_text: With 'O <s>Anumati</s>, give permission,' he sprinkles from the west toward the north.

children.text: sarasvate 'numanyasva ity uttarataḥ prācīnam ||
children.translated_text: With 'O <s>Sarasvatī</s>, give permission,' he sprinkles from the north toward the east.

children.text: deva savitaḥ prasuva iti samantaṃ pradakṣiṇaṃ samantam eva vā tūṣṇīm ||
children.translated_text: With 'God <s>Savitṛ</s>, impel,' he sprinkles all around clockwise; or he may do the whole circuit silently.

children.text: athebhyam abhyajya parisamidhaṃ śinaṣṭi svāhākāreṇābhyādhāyāghārāv ādhārayati ||
children.translated_text: Then, having anointed the fuel for them, he trims it, places it on the fire with the exclamation svāhā, and pours the two āghāra libations.

children.text: prajāpataye svāhā iti manasottare paridhisandhau saṃspṛśyākṣṇayā santatam ||
children.translated_text: With 'To <s>Prajāpati</s>, svāhā,' silently, he touches the northern junction of the enclosing sticks and pours continuously crosswise.

children.text: indrāya svāhā ity upāṃśu dakṣiṇe paridhisandhau saṃspṛśyākṣṇayā santatam ||
children.translated_text: With 'To <s>Indra</s>, svāhā,' in a low voice, he touches the southern junction of the enclosing sticks and pours continuously crosswise.

children.text: athājyabhāgau juhoti ||
children.translated_text: Then he offers the two portions of ghee.

children.text: agnaye svāhā ity uttarārdhapūrvārdhe ||
children.translated_text: With 'To <s>Agni</s>, svāhā,' in the eastern half of the northern half.

children.text: somāya svāhā iti dakṣiṇārdhapūrvārdhe ||
children.translated_text: With 'To <s>Soma</s>, svāhā,' in the eastern half of the southern half.

children.text: athāgnimukhaṃ juhoti ||
children.translated_text: Then he offers the agnimukha oblation.

children.text: yukto vaha jātavedaḥ purastād agne viddhi karma kriyamāṇaṃ yathedam
children.translated_text: 'Harnessed, carry it, O <s>Jātavedas</s>; O <s>Agni</s>, know beforehand the rite that is being performed here.

children.text: tvaṃ bhiṣagbheṣajasyāsi kartā tvayā gā aśvān puruṣān sanemi svāhā ||
children.translated_text: You are the physician and maker of the remedy; through you may we win cows, horses, and men. Svāhā.'

children.text: catasra āśāḥ pracarantv agnaya imaṃ no yajñaṃ nayatu prajānan
children.translated_text: 'Let the fires move through the four quarters; let the one who knows lead this sacrifice of ours,

children.text: ghṛtaṃ pibann ajaraṃ suvīraṃ brahma samidbhavaty āhutīnāṃ svāhā ||
children.translated_text: drinking ghee, undecaying, rich in heroes; the sacred formulation becomes the kindling of the oblations. Svāhā.'

children.text: ā no bhadrāḥ kratavo yantu viśvato 'dabdhāso aparītāsa udbhidaḥ
children.translated_text: 'May auspicious intentions come to us from every side, unassailable, unobstructed, breaking through.'

children.text: devā no yathā sadamidvṛdhe san na prāyuvo rakṣitāro dive dive svāhā ||
children.translated_text: May the gods be for our continual increase, unfailing protectors day by day. Svāhā.

children.text: virūpākṣa mā vibāṃdhiṣṭhā mā vibādha vibādhithāḥ
children.translated_text: O <s>Virūpākṣa</s>, do not obstruct me; do not injure me, you who have injured.

children.text: nirṛtyai tvā putram āhus sa naḥ marmāṇi dhāraya svāhā ||
children.translated_text: They call you the son of <s>Nirṛti</s>; hold fast our vital points. Svāhā.

children.text: virūpākṣam ahaṃ yaje nijaṅghaṃ śabaﾱodaram
children.translated_text: I sacrifice to <s>Virūpākṣa</s>, low-legged, with a mottled belly.

children.text: yo māyaṃ paribādhate śriyai puṣṭyai ca nityadā tasmai svāhā ||
children.translated_text: To him who constantly obstructs this of mine, for prosperity and nourishment, svāhā.

children.text: yā tiraścī nipadyase 'haṃ vigharaṇī iti
children.translated_text: You who lie crosswise, saying, 'I am the scatterer,'

children.text: tāṃ tvā ghṛtasya dhārayā 'gnau saṃrādhirnī yaje svāhā ||
children.translated_text: you I sacrifice in the fire, propitiating you with a stream of ghee. Svāhā.

children.text: saṃrādhinyai devyai svāhā
children.translated_text: To the goddess <s>Saṃrādhinī</s>, svāhā.

children.text: prasādhinyai denyai svāhā
children.translated_text: To the goddess <s>Prasādhinī</s>, svāhā.

children.text: bhūs svāhā
children.translated_text: For earth, svāhā.

children.text: bhuvas svāhā
children.translated_text: For midspace, svāhā.

children.text: suvas svāhā bhūr bhuvas suvas svāhā ity etāvat sarvadarvīhomānām eṣa kalpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For heaven, svāhā; for earth, midspace, and heaven, svāhā. This much is the rule for all ladle-offerings.

children.text: Chapter 4
athāsyā upotthāya dakṣiṇena hastena dakṣiṇam aṃsaṃ pratibāhum anvavahṛtya hṛdayadeśam abhimṛśati mama hṛdaye hṛdayaṃ te astu mama citte cittam astu te
children.translated_text: Then, standing up beside her, with his right hand he passes over her right shoulder toward the arm and touches the region of her heart: 'Let your heart be in my heart; let your mind be in my mind.'

children.text: mama vājam ekamanāḥ śṛṇu mām evānuvratā sahacaryā mayā bhava iti ||
children.translated_text: 'With one mind, listen to my vigor; be devoted to me alone, a companion with me.'

children.text: athāsyai dakṣiṇe karṇe japati ||
children.translated_text: Then he murmurs into her right ear.

children.text: māṃ te manaḥ praviśatu māṃ cakṣur mām u te bhagaḥ mayi sarvāṇi bhūtāni mayi prajñānam astu te ||
children.translated_text: 'Let your mind enter me, your eye into me, and your fortune into me. Let all beings be in me; let your understanding be in me.'

children.text: madhuge madhvagāhe jihvā me madhuvādinī
children.translated_text: 'O honey-going one, honey-plunging one, my tongue is honey-speaking.'

children.text: mukhe me sāraghaṃ madhu datsu saṃvananaṃ kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: 'In my mouth is bee-made honey; in my teeth conciliation has been made.'

children.text: cākravākaṃ saṃvananaṃ yan nadībhya udāhṛtam
children.translated_text: 'The cakravāka conciliation which was brought up from the rivers,'

children.text: yadvittau devagandharvau tena saṃvaninau svaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'and what the two divine <s>Gandharvas</s> know: by that may we two be mutually conciliating.'

children.text: spṛśāmi te 'ham aṅgāni vāyur āpaś ca mā maraḥ
children.translated_text: 'I touch your limbs; may wind and waters not kill me.'

children.text: māṃ caiva paśya sūryaṃ ca mā cānyeṣu manaḥkṛthāḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Look at me and at the sun, and do not set your mind on others.'

children.text: somaḥ prathamo vivide gandharvo vivida uttaraḥ
children.translated_text: '<s>Soma</s> first found you; the <s>Gandharva</s> found you next.'

children.text: tṛtīyo 'gniṣ ṭe patis turīyas te manuṣyajāḥ ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Agni</s> was your third husband; the fourth is born of men.'

children.text: somo 'dadad gandharvāya gandharvo 'dad agnaye
children.translated_text: '<s>Soma</s> gave her to the <s>Gandharva</s>; the <s>Gandharva</s> gave her to <s>Agni</s>.'

children.text: rayiṃ ca putrāṃś cādād agnir mahyam atho imām ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Agni</s> gave wealth and sons, and then this woman, to me.'

children.text: sarasvati predam ava subhage vājinīvati
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Sarasvatī</s>, favor this, fortunate one, rich in prizes.'

children.text: tāṃ tvā viśvasya bhūtasya pragāyāasyagrataḥ iti ||
children.translated_text: 'You, at the forefront of all that exists, I proclaim.'

children.text: athāsyai dakṣiṇena nīcā hastena dakṣiṇam uttānaṃ hastaṃ sāṅguṣṭham abhīva lomāni gṛhṇāti gṛbhṇāmi te suprajāstvāya hastaṃ mayā patyā jaradaṣṭir yathāsaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, with his right hand held downward, he takes her right hand, held upward and including the thumb, against the direction of the hair: 'I take your hand for good offspring, so that you may grow old with me as your husband.'

children.text: bhago 'ryamā savitā purandhir mahyaṃ tvādurgārhapatyāya devāḥ iti ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Bhaga</s>, <s>Aryaman</s>, <s>Savitṛ</s>, and <s>Purandhi</s>, the gods, have given you to me for householdership.'

children.text: athaināṃ pradakṣiṇam agniṃ paryāṇayati paritvāgne puraṃ vayaṃ vipraṃ sahasya dhīmahi
children.translated_text: Then he leads her clockwise around the fire: 'Around you, O <s>Agni</s>, we set the strong inspired one as a fortress.'

children.text: dhṛṣadvarṇaṃ divedive bhettāraṃ bhaṅgurāvataḥ iti ||
children.translated_text: 'Day by day, firm-colored, breaker of the brittle one.'

children.text: atha tathopaviśyānvārabdhāyām upayamanīr juhoti ||
children.translated_text: Then, having sat down in the same way while she has taken hold of him, he offers the upayamana oblations.

children.text: agne śardha mahate saubhagāya tava dyumnāny uttamāni santu
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Agni</s>, exert yourself for great good fortune; may your highest splendors be present.'

children.text: sañ jāspatyaṃ suyamam ākṛṇuṣva śatrūyatām abhitiṣṭhā mahāṃsi svāhā ||
children.translated_text: 'Make the union of husband and wife well controlled; stand over the great powers of those who act as enemies. Svāhā.'

children.text: somāya janivide svāhā ||
children.translated_text: 'To <s>Soma</s>, knower of wives, svāhā.'

children.text: gandharvāya janivide svāhā ||
children.translated_text: 'To the <s>Gandharva</s>, knower of wives, svāhā.'

children.text: agnaye janivide svāhā ||
children.translated_text: 'To <s>Agni</s>, knower of wives, svāhā.'

children.text: kanyalā pitṛbhyo yatī patilokam av dīkṣām adāstha svāhā ||
children.translated_text: 'The maiden, going from her fathers to the world of her husband, has given consecration. Svāhā.'

children.text: preto muñcāti nāmutas subaddhām amutas karat
children.translated_text: 'Let him release her from here, not from there; let him make her well bound from there.'

children.text: yatheyam indra mīḍhvas suputrā subhagā satī svāhā ||
children.translated_text: 'So that she here, O generous <s>Indra</s>, may be blessed with good sons and good fortune. Svāhā.'

children.text: imāṃ tvam indra mīḍhvas suputrāṃ subhagāṃ kuru
children.translated_text: 'Make this woman, O generous <s>Indra</s>, blessed with good sons and good fortune.'

children.text: daśāsyāṃ putrān ādhehi patim ekādaśaṃ svāhā ||
children.translated_text: 'Place ten sons in her; make her husband the eleventh. Svāhā.'

children.text: agnir aitu prathamo devatānāṃ so 'syai prajāṃ muñcatu mṛtyupāśāt
children.translated_text: 'Let <s>Agni</s>, first of the deities, come; let him release her offspring from the noose of death.'

children.text: tad ayaṃ strī pautram aghaṃ na rodāt svāhā ||
children.translated_text: 'May this woman not weep over harm to a grandson. Svāhā.'

children.text: imām agnis trāyatāṃ gārhapatyaḥ prajām asyai nayatu dīrgham āyuḥ
children.translated_text: 'May <s>Agni Gārhapatya</s> protect this woman; may he lead her offspring to long life.'

children.text: aśūnyopasthā jīvatām astu mātā pautram ānandam abhiprabudhyatām iyaṃ svāhā ||
children.translated_text: 'May the mother live with an unempty lap; may this woman awaken to the joy of a grandson. Svāhā.'

children.text: mā te gṛhe niśi ghoṣa utthād anyatra tvad rudatyas saṃviśantu
children.translated_text: 'May no cry arise in your house at night; let weeping women lie down elsewhere, away from you.'

children.text: mā tvaṃ vikeśyura āvadhiṣṭhā jīvapaīn patiloke virāja paśyantī prajāṃ sumanasyamānāṃ svāhā ||
children.translated_text: 'Do not, disheveled, strike your breast; shine in your husband's world with living husband, seeing your offspring and being well-minded. Svāhā.'

children.text: aprajastāṃ pautramṛtyuṃ pāpmānam uta vāgham
children.translated_text: 'Childlessness, death of a grandson, evil, and also sin,'

children.text: śīrṣṇas srajam ivonmucya dviṣadbhyaḥ pratimuñcāmi pāśaṃ svāhā iti ||
children.translated_text: 'unfastening it from the head like a garland, I fasten the noose upon those who hate us. Svāhā.'

children.text: athainām utthāpyottareṇāgniṃ dakṣiṇena padā 'śmānam āsthāpayati ātiṣṭhemam aśmānam aśmeva tvaṃ sthirā bhava
children.translated_text: Then, having raised her up, to the north of the fire he makes her step with her right foot on a stone: 'Step upon this stone; be firm like a stone.'

children.text: abhitiṣṭha pṛtanyatas sahasva pṛtanāyataḥ iti ||
children.translated_text: 'Stand firm against those who attack; withstand those who wage battle.'

children.text: athāsyā añjalāv upastīrya tasyās sodaryo dvir lājān āvapati ||
children.translated_text: Then, after he has strewn into her joined hands, her own brother pours parched grain twice into them.

children.text: tān abhidhārya juhoti iyaṃ nāry upabrūte 'gnau lājān āvapantī
children.translated_text: Having held them over the fire, he offers: 'This woman speaks while pouring parched grain into the fire.'

children.text: dīrghāyus astu me patir jīvātu śaradaś śataṃ svāhā ||
children.translated_text: 'May my husband be long-lived; may he live a hundred autumns. Svāhā.'

children.text: athaināṃ pradakṣiṇam agniṃ paryāṇayati tubhyam agne paryavahan sūryāṃ vahatunā saha
children.translated_text: Then he leads her clockwise around the fire: 'For you, O <s>Agni</s>, they carried <s>Sūryā</s> around together with the bridal procession.'

children.text: punaḥ patibhyo jāyāṃ dā agne prajayā saha iti ||
children.translated_text: 'Give the wife again to her husbands, O <s>Agni</s>, together with offspring.'

children.text: tathāsthāpayati tathā juhoti ||
children.translated_text: He makes her stand in the same way, and offers in the same way.

children.text: athaināṃ punaḥ pradakṣiṇam agniṃ paryāṇayati punaḥ patnīm agnir adād āyuṣā saha varcasā
children.translated_text: Then again he leads her clockwise around the fire: '<s>Agni</s> has again given the wife together with life and brilliance.'

children.text: dīrghāyur asyā yaḥ patis sa etu śaradaś śatam iti ||
children.translated_text: 'May the husband of this woman be long-lived; may he reach a hundred autumns.'

children.text: tathaivāsthāpayati tathaiva juhoti ||
children.translated_text: He makes her stand in just the same way and offers in just the same way.

children.text: athaināṃ punar eva paryāṇayati viśvā uta tvayā vayaṃ dhārā udanyā iva
children.translated_text: Then he leads her around once again, saying: 'All hostility, indeed, with you may we cross over, like streams over a thirsty place,'

children.text: atigāhemahi dviṣaḥ iti ||
children.translated_text: 'may we pass beyond hatreds,' thus.

children.text: atha tathopaviśyānvarabdhāyāṃ jayān abhyātānān rāṣṭrabhṛta iti hutvā athāmātyahomān juhoti ||
children.translated_text: Then, having sat down in the same way, while she has taken hold of him, after offering the <s>Jayā</s>, <s>Abhyātāna</s>, and <s>Rāṣṭrabhṛt</s> oblations, he then offers the <s>amātya</s> oblations.

children.text: atha prājāpatyāt juhoti prajāpate na tvad etāny anyaḥ iti ||
children.translated_text: Then he offers from the <s>Prājāpatya</s> portion, saying: '<s>Prajāpati</s>, no one other than you has encompassed these things,' and so on.

children.text: atha sauviṣṭakṛtaṃ juhoti yad asya karmaṇo 'tyarīricaṃ yad vā nyūnam ihākaram
children.translated_text: Then he offers the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> oblation: 'Whatever has been excessive in this rite, or whatever deficiency I have made here,

children.text: agnis tat sviṣṭakṛd vidvān sarvaṃ sviṣṭaṃ suhutaṃ karotu me
children.translated_text: may <s>Agni</s>, the wise <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s>, make all that well performed and well offered for me.

children.text: agnaye sviṣṭakṛte suhutahuta āhutīnāṃ kāmānāṃ samardhayitre svāhā iti ||
children.translated_text: To <s>Agni Sviṣṭakṛt</s>, who makes the well-offered oblations effective for the desired aims, svāhā,' thus.

children.text: atha sruveṇa paridhīn anakti ||
children.translated_text: Then with the offering spoon he anoints the enclosing sticks.

children.text: atha paristarāt samullipyājyasthālyāṃ prastaravat barhir aktvā tṛṇaṃ pracchādyāgnāv anupraharati ||
children.translated_text: Then, having taken up some from the strewn grass, having anointed the barhis in the ghee-pot like the prastara, and having covered it with grass, he throws it after into the fire.

children.text: atha śamyā apohya tathaiva pariṣiñcati
children.translated_text: Then, having removed the śamyā sticks, he sprinkles around in just the same way,

children.text: anvamaṃsthāḥ prāsāvīḥ iti mantrān tān sannamayati ||
children.translated_text: and he brings together those mantras, 'You have assented; you have brought forth,' and so on.

children.text: atha praṇotādbhyo diśo vyunnīya brahmaṇe varaṃ dadāmīti gāṃ brāhmaṇebhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, having poured out from the praṇīta waters toward the directions, saying, 'I give the chosen gift to the brahman,' he gives a cow to the Brahmins.

children.text: eṣa āghārabān darvīhomaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This is the ladle-offering with āghāra.

children.text: athāparaḥ parisamūhya paryukṣya paristīryājyaṃ vilāpyotpūya struk struvaṃ niṣṭapya saṃmṛjya sruci caturgṛhītaṃ gṛhītvā sarvān mantrān samanudrutya sakṛd evāhutiṃ juhoti ||
children.translated_text: Now another: having swept around, sprinkled around, strewn grass, melted and purified the ghee, heated and wiped the ladle and spoon, taken four scoopfuls in the ladle, and run through all the mantras together, he offers just one oblation.

children.text: agnis sviṣṭakṛd dvitīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Agni Sviṣṭakṛt</s> is the second.

children.text: dvir juhoti dvir nimārṣṭi dviḥ prāśnāty utsṛpyācāmati nirleḍhīty eṣa āgnihotrikaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He offers twice, wipes twice, eats twice, sips after moving away, and licks clean: this is the <s>āgnihotrika</s> form.

children.text: athāparaḥ parisamūhya paryukṣya paristīrya prākṛtena haviṣā yāvad āmnātam āhutīr juhoty eṣa hy apūrvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now another: having swept around, sprinkled around, and strewn grass, he offers the oblations as far as they are prescribed, with the ordinary oblation-material; for this is an independent rite.

children.text: tatrodāharanti āghāraṃ prakṛtiṃ prāha darvīhomasya bādariḥ
children.translated_text: On this they cite: '<s>Bādari</s> declares āghāra to be the model for the ladle-offering,

children.text: āgnihotrikaṃ tathātreyaḥ kāśakṛtsnas tv apūrvatām iti ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Ātreya</s> likewise the <s>āgnihotrika</s>; but <s>Kāśakṛtsna</s> declares its independence,' thus.

children.text: Chapter 5
vijñāte garbhe tipye puṃsavanam ||
children.translated_text: When pregnancy is recognized, under <s>Tiṣya</s>, the <s>puṃsavana</s> is performed.

children.text: brāhmaṇānannena pariviṣya puṇyāhaṃ svasti ṛddhimiti vācayitvā ||
children.translated_text: Having served Brahmins with food, he has them pronounce 'auspicious day, welfare, prosperity.'

children.text: atha devayajanollekhanaprabhṛtyā 'gnimukhāt kṛtvā pakvājjuhoti prajāpate tanvaṃ me juṣasva tvaṣṭar devebhiḥ sahasāma indra
children.translated_text: Then, beginning with the marking out of the divine sacrificial place, having performed the fire-preparation, he offers from cooked food: '<s>Prajāpati</s>, favor my body; <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, together with the gods, with power; <s>Indra</s>,

children.text: viśvairdevairātibhiḥ saṃrarāṇaḥ puṃsāṃ bahūnāṃ mātaraḥ syāma svāhā iti ||
children.translated_text: 'uniting with all the gods as helpers, may we become mothers of many males, svāhā,' thus.

children.text: athājyāhutīrupajuhoti garbho 'syoṣadhīnāṃ garbho vanaspatīnām iti tisṛbhir anucchandasam ||
children.translated_text: Then he offers ghee oblations with the three verses beginning 'He is the embryo of the herbs, the embryo of the forest trees,' without regard to metre.

children.text: sviṣṭakṛtprabhṛti siddham ā dhenuvarapradānāt ||
children.translated_text: From the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> onward, the procedure is established up to the giving of the cow as the chosen gift.

children.text: athāsyā ājyaśeṣamāsye pracyotayatyasme devāso vapuṣe cikitsata iti catasṛbhir anucchandasam ||
children.translated_text: Then he lets the remainder of the ghee drip into her mouth with the four verses beginning 'May the gods attend to us for bodily beauty,' without regard to metre.

children.text: Chapter 6
tāṃ na mithas saṃsādayed anādeśāt ||
children.translated_text: They should not cause her to come together in intercourse except by instruction.

children.text: anunayanty etam agnim ||
children.translated_text: They conciliate this fire.

children.text: athaināṃ pitur aṅkād udvahati guror vā ye vadhvaś candraṃ vahatuṃ yakṣmā yanti janāṃū anu
children.translated_text: Then he leads her away from the lap of her father, or of her teacher, saying: 'Those wasting diseases that follow the bride's lunar conveyance among people,

children.text: punas tān yajñikīyā devā nayantu yata āgatāḥ iti ||
children.translated_text: may the sacrificial gods lead them back again to the place from which they came,' thus.

children.text: athaināṃ dakṣiṇe haste gṛhītvā svaratham āropya svān gṛhān ānayati pūṣā tveto nayatu hastagṛhyāśvinau tvā pravahatāṃ rathena
children.translated_text: Then, having taken her by the right hand, placed her on his own chariot, and brought her to his own house, he says: 'May <s>Pūṣan</s> lead you from here, taking your hand; may the two <s>Aśvins</s> carry you forth by chariot.

children.text: gṛhān gaccha gṛhapatnī yathāso vaśinī tvaṃ vidathamāvadāsi iti ||
children.translated_text: Go to the houses, so that you may be mistress of the house; as one with control, speak in the assembly,' thus.

children.text: panthānam anumantrayate su gaṃ panthānam ārukṣam ariṣṭaṃ svastivāhanam
children.translated_text: He addresses the road with a mantra: 'I have mounted a good road, unharmed and bearing welfare,

children.text: yasmin vīro na riṣyaty anyeṣāṃ vindate vasu iti ||
children.translated_text: on which the hero does not suffer harm and finds the wealth of others,' thus.

children.text: oṣadhivanaspatayo nadyo vanāny anumantrayate yā oṣadhayo yā vanaspatayo yā nadyo yāni dhanvāni ye vanā
children.translated_text: He addresses the herbs, forest trees, rivers, and forests with a mantra: 'The herbs, the forest trees, the rivers, the deserts, and the forests,

children.text: te tvā vadhu prajāvatīṃ pratve muñcantv aṃhasaḥ iti ||
children.translated_text: may they release you, bride, rich in offspring, from distress,' thus.

children.text: atha jāyām ānīya svān gṛhān prapādayati bhadrān gṛhān sumanasaḥ prapadye 'vīgghnī vīravatas suvīrān
children.translated_text: Then, having brought his wife, he makes her enter his own house: 'I enter auspicious houses, kindly disposed, unharmed, rich in heroes and good sons,

children.text: irāṃ vahato ghṛtam ukṣamāṇās teṣv ahaṃ sumanās saṃviśāni iti ||
children.translated_text: bearing refreshment and sprinkling ghee; among them may I settle with a kindly mind,' thus.

children.text: athainām ānaḍuhe carmaṇy upaveśayati iha gāvaḥ prajāyadhvam ihāśvā iha pūruṣāḥ
children.translated_text: Then he seats her on the hide of a red ox, saying: 'Here may cows be born, here horses, here men;

children.text: iho sahasradakṣiṇo rāyaspoṣo niṣīdatu iti ||
children.translated_text: here may wealth and nourishment, with a thousand gifts, sit down,' thus.

children.text: atrābhyām amātyās stokmāṇy āropayante ||
children.translated_text: There the relatives place handfuls of grain upon the two of them.

children.text: atha vācaṃ yacchataḥ ā nakṣatrāṇām udayāt ||
children.translated_text: Then the two keep silence until the rising of the constellations.

children.text: athāhorātrayos sandhim anumantrayate nīlalohite bhavataḥ kṛtyāsaktir vyajyate
children.translated_text: Then he addresses the junction of day and night with a mantra: 'You two become dark-blue and red; the attachment of sorcery is made manifest.

children.text: edhante 'syā jñātayaḥ patir bandheṣu badhyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: May her kinsmen prosper; may her husband be bound among his kin,' thus.

children.text: athoditeṣu nakṣatreṣūpaniṣkramya dhruvam arundhatīṃ ca darśayati ||
children.translated_text: Then, when the constellations have risen, having gone out, he shows her <s>Dhruva</s> and <s>Arundhatī</s>.

children.text: dhruvo 'si dhruvakṣitir dhruvam asi dhruvatas sthitam
children.translated_text: For <s>Dhruva</s>: 'You are fixed; your dwelling is fixed; you are fixed, standing in fixedness.

children.text: tvaṃ nakṣatrāṇāṃ methy asi sa mā pāhi pṛtanyataḥ iti dhruvam ||
children.translated_text: You are the central post of the constellations; protect me from hostile attack,' thus.

children.text: sapta ṛṣayaḥ prathamāṃ kṛttikānām arundhatīṃ yad dhruvatāṃ ha ninyuḥ
children.translated_text: For <s>Arundhatī</s>: 'When the seven seers, first among the <s>Kṛttikās</s>, led <s>Arundhatī</s> to fixedness,

children.text: ṣaṭkṛttikā mukhyayogaṃ vahantīyam asmākam edhatv aṣṭamy arundhatī ity arundhatīm ||
children.translated_text: she, the eighth <s>Arundhatī</s>, bearing the principal conjunction of the six <s>Kṛttikās</s>, may she prosper for us,' thus.

children.text: atha vivāhasyārundhaty upasthānāt kṛtvā vratam upaiti agne vratapate upayamanaṃ vrataṃ cariṣyāmi tac chakeyaṃ tan me rādhyatām
children.translated_text: Then, beginning from the attendance upon <s>Arundhatī</s> in the marriage rite, he undertakes a vow: '<s>Agni</s>, lord of vows, I shall observe the vow of taking by the hand; may I be able to do it; may it succeed for me.'

children.text: vāyo vratapata āditya vratapate vratānāṃ vratapate upayananaṃ vrataṃ cariṣyāmi tac chakeyaṃ tan me rādhyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vāyu</s>, lord of vows; <s>Āditya</s>, lord of vows; lord of the vows among vows: I shall observe the vow of leading forth; may I be able to do it; may it succeed for me, thus.

children.text: ubhau jāyāpatī vratacāriṇau brahmacāriṇau bhavato 'dhaśśayāte ||
children.translated_text: Both husband and wife become vow-observers and brahmacārins; they sleep below.

children.text: tayoś śyām antareṇodumbaradaṇḍo gandhānulipto vāsasā sūtreṇa vā parivītas tiṣṭhaty āpakvahomāt ||
children.translated_text: Between the two of them, in the space between, an udumbara staff, anointed with fragrances and wrapped with a garment or with a cord, stands until the cooked oblation.

children.text: caturthyāṃ niśāyāṃ hute pakvahome vrataṃ visṛjya daṇḍam utthāpayatyūrjaḥ pṛthivyā adhyutthito 'si vanaspate śatavalśo viroha
children.translated_text: On the fourth night, when the cooked oblation has been offered, having released the vow, he raises up the staff, saying: 'You have risen up from the vigor of the earth, O forest tree; grow with a hundred shoots.

children.text: tvayā vayam iṣam ūrja vadanto rāyaspoṣeṇa samiṣā madema iti ||
children.translated_text: Through you may we, speaking of refreshment and vigor, rejoice in prosperity rich in wealth and nourishment,' thus.

children.text: athainaṃ vadhvai prayacchati prajayā tvā saṃsṛjāmi māsareṇa surām iva iti ||
children.translated_text: Then he gives it to the bride, saying: 'I join you with offspring, like liquor with the fermenting mash,' thus.

children.text: taṃ vadhūḥ pratigṛhṇāti prajāvatī bhūyāsam iti ||
children.translated_text: The bride receives it, saying: 'May I become possessed of offspring,' thus.

children.text: athainaṃ varāya prayacchati prajayā tvā paśubhis saṃsṛjāmi māsareṇa surām iva iti ||
children.translated_text: Then he gives it to the bridegroom, saying: 'I join you with offspring and cattle, like liquor with the fermenting mash,' thus.

children.text: taṃ varaḥ pratigṛhṇāti prajāvān paśumān bhūyāsam iti ||
children.translated_text: The bridegroom receives it, saying: 'May I become possessed of offspring and cattle,' thus.

children.text: athainaṃ sthūṇādeśe nidhāyāntikena pratipadyate ||
children.translated_text: Then, having placed it in the position of a post, he proceeds with what is near at hand.

children.text: prasiddham upasaṃveśanam ||
children.translated_text: The lying down together is as already established.

children.text: śvobhūte daṇḍam ādāya puṇyāhaṃ vācayitvāpsu visarjayati ||
children.translated_text: On the next day, having taken the staff and having caused the auspicious-day proclamation to be made, he casts it into the waters.

children.text: atha devayajanollekhanaprabhṛtyāgnimutvāt kṛtvā pakvāj juhoti agnir mūrdhā bhuvaḥ iti dvābhyām ||
children.translated_text: Then, beginning with the marking out of the divine sacrificial place, having performed the fire-preparation, he offers from cooked food with the two verses beginning '<s>Agni</s> is the head of the earth.'

children.text: sviṣṭakṛtprabhṛti siddham ādhenuvarapradānāt ||
children.translated_text: From the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> onward, the procedure is established up to the giving of the cow as the chosen gift.

children.text: sa eṣa pārvaṇo bhavati ||
children.translated_text: This is the fortnightly form.

children.text: athāstamita āditye 'nyonyam alaṅkṛtyopariśayyāṃ śayāte ||
children.translated_text: Then, when the sun has set, having adorned one another, they lie on the upper couch.

children.text: atha vadhūm abhimantrayate sumaṅgalīr iyaṃ vadhūr imāṃ sameta paśyata
children.translated_text: Then he addresses the bride with the mantra: 'This bride is auspicious; come together and look upon her.

children.text: saubhāgyam asyai datvāyāthāstaṃ viparetana iti ||
children.translated_text: Having bestowed good fortune upon her, go back each to your own house,' thus.

children.text: athaināṃ sarvasurabhigandhayā mālayā yunakti saṃ nā manas saṃ hṛdayāni saṃ nābhi saṃ tanutyajaḥ
children.translated_text: Then he joins her with a garland fragrant with all perfumes, saying: 'Together be our minds, together our hearts, together our navels, together what leaves the body.

children.text: saṃ tvā kāmasya yākreṇe yuñjaty avimocanāya iti ||
children.translated_text: With the bond of desire he joins you for non-separation,' thus.

children.text: Chapter 7
prathamagarbhāyāś caturthe māsi sīmantonnayanam ||
children.translated_text: In the fourth month of a first pregnancy is the <s>sīmantonnayana</s> (parting of the hair).

children.text: brāhmaṇān annena pariviṣya puṇyāhaṃ svasti ṛddhim iti vācayitvā ||
children.translated_text: Having served Brahmins with food, he has them pronounce 'auspicious day, welfare, prosperity.'

children.text: atha devayajanollekhanaprabhṛtyāgnimukhāt kṛtvā pakvāj juhoti ||
children.translated_text: Then, beginning with the marking out of the divine sacrificial place, having performed the fire-preparation, he offers from cooked food.

children.text: dhātā dadātu naḥ iti puronuvākyām anūcya dhātā prajāyā uta rāya īśe iti yājyayā juhoti ||
children.translated_text: Having recited '<s>Dhātṛ</s> should give to us' as the invitatory verse, he offers with the offering verse '<s>Dhātṛ</s> rules over offspring and wealth.'

children.text: athājyāhutīr upajuhoti dhātā dadātu no rayiṃ prācīm ity ā antād anuvākasya ||
children.translated_text: Then he offers supplementary ghee oblations, beginning with '<s>Dhātṛ</s> should give us wealth facing forward,' up to the end of the anuvāka.

children.text: sviṣṭakṛtprabhṛti siddham ā dhenuvarapradānāt ||
children.translated_text: From the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> onward, the procedure is established up to the giving of the cow as the chosen gift.

children.text: athāsyās treṇyā śalalyā tribhir darbhapuñjīlair udumbaraprasūnair yavaprasūnair iti keśān vibhajan sīmantam unnayati rākām aham yās te rāke iti dvābhyām ||
children.translated_text: Then, with a threefold porcupine quill, with three bunches of darbha, with udumbara blossoms and barley blossoms, he parts her hair and raises the parting, using the two verses beginning '<s>Rākā</s>, I invoke' and 'What is yours, O <s>Rākā</s>.'

children.text: athāsyai yavaprasūnāny ābadhnāti yavo 'si yavayāsmaddveṣo yavayārātīḥ iti ||
children.translated_text: Then he ties barley blossoms onto her, saying: 'You are barley; drive away hatred from us; drive away enemies,' thus.

children.text: athainau vīṇāgāthināv iti pratigṛhṇīte ||
children.translated_text: Then he receives these two, a vīṇā-player and a singer.

children.text: athainau saṃśāsti gāyatam iti ||
children.translated_text: Then he instructs the two: 'Sing,' thus.

children.text: tāv etāṃ gāthāṃ gāyataḥ soma eva no rājety āhur brāhmaṇīḥ prajāḥ
children.translated_text: The two sing this song: 'The Brahmin women say, "<s>Soma</s> alone is our king."

children.text: vivṛttacakrā āsīnās tīreṇāsau tava iti ||
children.translated_text: Sitting with the wheel turned apart, on the bank is so-and-so, yours,' thus.

children.text: yasyai nadyās tīre saṃśritā vasanti tasyai nāma gṛhṇāti ||
children.translated_text: He takes the name of the river on whose bank settled people dwell.

children.text: aṣṭame māsi viṣṇava āhutīr juhoti viṣṇor nu kam ity etena sūktena ||
children.translated_text: In the eighth month he offers oblations to <s>Viṣṇu</s> with this hymn beginning '<s>Viṣṇu</s>, now indeed.'

children.text: viṣṇave balim upaharati ||
children.translated_text: He presents a bali offering to <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: vaiṣṇavo hy eṣa māso vijñāyate ||
children.translated_text: For this month is known to belong to <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: viṣṇur hi garbhasya devatā ||
children.translated_text: For <s>Viṣṇu</s> is the deity of the embryo.

children.text: iti huto vyākhyātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The offering having thus been made has been explained.

children.text: Chapter 8
yathaitaddhute baliharaṇam ||
children.translated_text: As, after this offering, there is the bringing of the bali.

children.text: viṣṇave baliraṣṭame māsi pūrvapakṣasya saptamyāṃ dvādaśyāṃ rohiṇyāṃ śroṇāyāṃ vā ||
children.translated_text: The bali to <s>Viṣṇu</s> is in the eighth month, on the seventh or twelfth day of the bright fortnight, or under <s>Rohiṇī</s> or <s>Śroṇā</s>.

children.text: brāhmaṇānannena pariviṣya puṇyāhaṃ svasti ṛddhimiti vācayitvā ||
children.translated_text: Having served Brahmins with food, he has them pronounce 'auspicious day, welfare, prosperity.'

children.text: atha devayajanollekhanaprabhṛtyā praṇītābhyaḥ kṛtvā upotthāyāgreṇāgniṃ daivatamāvāhayati oṃ bhūḥ puruṣamāvāhayāmi oṃ bhuvaḥ puruṣamāvāhayāmi oṃ suvaḥ puruṣamāvāhayāmi oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ suvaḥ puruṣamāvāhayāmi ityāvāhya ||
children.translated_text: Then, beginning with the marking out of the divine sacrificial place, after preparing as far as the praṇīta waters, having risen up, he invokes the deity in front of the fire: 'Om bhūḥ, I invoke <s>Puruṣa</s>; om bhuvaḥ, I invoke <s>Puruṣa</s>; om suvaḥ, I invoke <s>Puruṣa</s>; om bhūr bhuvaḥ suvaḥ, I invoke <s>Puruṣa</s>,' thus having invoked him.

children.text: paridhānaprabhṛtyā 'gnimukhātkṛtvā daivatamarcayati ||
children.translated_text: Beginning with the paridhāna, after performing the fire-preparation, he worships the deity.

children.text: āpo hiṣṭhā mayobhuvaḥ iti tisṛbhiḥ hiraṇyavarṇāḥ śucayaḥ pāvakāḥ iti catasṛbhiḥ pavamānaḥ suvarjanaḥ ityetenānuvākena mārjayitvā ||
children.translated_text: Having cleansed himself with waters using the three verses beginning 'Waters, you are indeed bringers of happiness,' the four beginning 'Golden-colored, pure, purifying,' and the anuvāka beginning '<s>Pavamāna</s>, winner of heaven,'

children.text: athādbhistarpayati keśavaṃ tarpayāmi nārāyaṇaṃ māghavaṃ govindaṃ viṣṇuṃ madhusūdanaṃ trivikramaṃ vāmanaṃ śrīdharaṃ hṛṣīkeśaṃ padmanābhaṃ dāmodaraṃ tarpayāmi iti ||
children.translated_text: then he satisfies him with waters: 'I satisfy <s>Keśava</s>; <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, <s>Mādhava</s>, <s>Govinda</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Madhusūdana</s>, <s>Trivikrama</s>, <s>Vāmana</s>, <s>Śrīdhara</s>, <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, <s>Padmanābha</s>, <s>Dāmodara</s>, I satisfy,' thus.

children.text: etaireva nāmadheyairgandhapuṣpadhūpadīpaiḥ amuṣmai namo 'muṣmai namaḥ ityabhyarcya ||
children.translated_text: With these very names, with fragrance, flowers, incense, and lamps, saying 'Homage to this one, homage to that one,' he worships them.

children.text: atha viṣṇava āhutīrjuhoti viṣṇornu kam tadasya priyam pra tad viṣṇuḥ paro mātrayā vicakrame trirdevaḥ iti ||
children.translated_text: Then he offers oblations to <s>Viṣṇu</s>: '<s>Viṣṇu</s>, now indeed'; 'That dear place of his'; 'That <s>Viṣṇu</s> strode forth'; 'Beyond measure the god stepped three times,' thus.

children.text: jayaprabhṛti siddham ā dhenuvarapradānāt ||
children.translated_text: From the <s>Jayā</s> offerings onward, the procedure is established up to the giving of the cow as the chosen gift.

children.text: atha guḍapāyasaṃ ghṛtamiśramannaṃ nivedayati amuṣmai svāhā namo 'muṣmai svāhā namaḥ iti dvādaśabhiryathāliṅgam ||
children.translated_text: Then he presents a food of molasses and milk-rice mixed with ghee, saying, according to each name, 'To this one, svāhā; homage. To that one, svāhā; homage,' with the twelve names.

children.text: vaiṣṇavībhiḥ ṛgyajuḥsāmātharvabhiḥ stotraiḥ stutibhiḥ stuvanti ||
children.translated_text: They praise him with Vaiṣṇava verses, with Ṛg, Yajus, Sāman, and Atharvan hymns, with songs of praise and laudations.

children.text: vyāhṛtībhiḥ puruṣamudvāsayāmītyudvāsyānnaśeṣaṃ patnīṃ prāśayet ||
children.translated_text: With the vyāhṛtis, saying, 'I lead <s>Puruṣa</s> forth,' having led him forth, he should make the wife eat all the remaining food.

children.text: pumānasyai jāyata iti vijñāyate ||
children.translated_text: It is known that a male child is born to her.

children.text: Chapter 9
atha prahutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now, the offering after birth.

children.text: jātaṃ kumāramabhimantrayate adbhyaḥ sambhūtaḥ ityetenānuvākena ||
children.translated_text: He addresses the boy who has been born with the anuvāka beginning 'Born from the waters.'

children.text: athainaṃ snapayati kṣetriyai tvā nirṛtyai tvā iti ṣaḍbhiranucchandasam ||
children.translated_text: Then he bathes him with the six verses beginning 'For freedom from disease I take you, from calamity I take you,' without changing the meter.

children.text: athainaṃ svopasthaṃ ādadhāti aṅgādaṅgātsambhavasi hṛdayādadhijāyase
children.translated_text: Then he places him in his own lap, saying, 'From limb to limb you come into being; from the heart you are born.

children.text: ātmā vai putranāmāsi saṃjīva śaradaḥ śatam iti ||
children.translated_text: You are truly the self under the name of son; live together with us for a hundred autumns,' thus.

children.text: athainaṃ mūrdhnyabhijighrati aśmā bhava paraśurbhava hiraṇyamastṛtaṃ bhava
children.translated_text: Then he smells him on the head, saying, 'Be a stone; be an axe; be gold unbroken.

children.text: paśūnāṃ tvā hiṅkāreṇābhijighrāmyasau iti nakṣatranāmadheyena ||
children.translated_text: With the lowing of cattle I smell you, so-and-so,' using the name from the lunar mansion.

children.text: athāsya dakṣiṇe karṇe japati agnirāyuṣmān iti pañcabhiḥ paryāyaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then he murmurs into his right ear the five repetitions beginning '<s>Agni</s> is long-lived.'

children.text: athainaṃ dadhimadhughṛtamiti samudāyutya hiraṇyena prāśayati prāṇo rakṣati viśvamejat ityetenānuvākena pratyṛcam ||
children.translated_text: Then, having mixed together curds, honey, and ghee, he makes him taste it with gold, verse by verse, with the anuvāka beginning '<s>Prāṇa</s> protects all that moves.'

children.text: atiśiṣṭaṃ gopade ninayati vyāhṛtībhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: He pours what is left at the foot of a cow, with the vyāhṛtis.

children.text: athainaṃ māturupastha ādadhāti sīda tvaṃ māturasyā upasthe iti catasṛbhiḥ sahaṃsābhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then he places him in the mother's lap with the four verses, together with the haṃsa verses, beginning 'Sit in the lap of this mother.'

children.text: stanamabhimantrayate yaste stanaḥ śaśayo yo mayobhūr yena viśvā puṣyasi vāryāṇi
children.translated_text: He addresses the breast: 'That breast of yours which lies there, which brings delight, with which you nourish all desirable things,

children.text: yo ratnadhā vasuvid yaḥ sudatraḥ sarasvati tamiha dhātave kaḥ iti ||
children.translated_text: which holds treasures, knows wealth, and gives good gifts, O <s>Sarasvatī</s>, bring that here for nursing,' thus.

children.text: dhayantamanumantrayate dyauste pṛṣṭhaṃ rakṣatu vāyurūrū aśvinau ca stanaṃ dhayantaṃ savitā 'bhirakṣatu
children.translated_text: As he sucks, he addresses him: 'May heaven protect your back, <s>Vāyu</s> your thighs, and the <s>Aśvins</s> the breast as you suck; may <s>Savitṛ</s> guard you.

children.text: āvāsasaḥ parighānād bṛhaspatirviśvedevā abhirakṣantu paścāt iti ||
children.translated_text: From the enclosure of the dwelling may <s>Bṛhaspati</s> guard you; may all the gods guard you from behind,' thus.

children.text: athāsyodakumbhamucchirasi nidadhāti āpaḥ supteṣu jāgrata rakṣāṃsi nīrito nudadhvam iti ||
children.translated_text: Then he places a water-pot above his head, saying, 'Waters, stay awake among those who sleep; drive away the demons sent here,' thus.

children.text: atha devayajanollekhanaprabhṛtyāgnimukhāt kṛtvā pakvājjuhoti hariṃ harantamanuyanti devāḥ iti puro 'nuvākyāmanūcya mā chido mṛtyo mā vadhīḥ iti yājyayā juhoti ||
children.translated_text: Then, beginning with the marking out of the divine sacrificial place and after performing the fire-preparation, he offers from cooked food; having recited as the invitatory verse 'The gods follow <s>Hari</s> as he carries away,' he offers with the offering verse 'Do not cut, O <s>Mṛtyu</s>; do not strike.'

children.text: athājyāhutīrupajuhoti sadyaścakamānāya ityāntād anuvākasya ||
children.translated_text: Then he offers supplementary ghee oblations, beginning with 'For the one desiring at once' up to the end of the anuvāka.

children.text: sviṣṭakṛtprabhṛti siddham ā dhenuvarapradānāt ||
children.translated_text: From the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> onward, the procedure is established up to the giving of the cow as the chosen gift.

children.text: athānoyugaṃ rathayugaṃ vā snāpyācchādyālaṃkṛtya agreṇāgnimuddhṛtya tasyāgreṇāśvatthaparṇeṣu hutaśeṣaṃ nidadhāti nama āvyādhinībhyaḥ iti ||
children.translated_text: Then, having bathed, clothed, and adorned an axle-yoke or chariot-yoke, and having taken it forward of the fire, he places the remains of the oblation on aśvattha leaves in front of it, saying, 'Homage to the piercing ones.'

children.text: athāstamita āditye gaurasarṣapān phalīkaraṇamiśrān añjalinā juhoti kṛṇuṣva pājaḥ prasitiṃ na pṛthvīm ityetenānuvākena pratyṛcam ||
children.translated_text: Then, when the sun has set, he offers, with a handful, white mustard seeds mixed with parched grain, verse by verse, using the anuvāka beginning 'Make your force like the spreading earth.'

children.text: athaudanam tilasaktubhir ghṛteneti samudāyutya goṣṭhe 'śvatthaparṇeṣu hutaśeṣaṃ nidadhāti aghorāya mahāghorāya namo namaḥ iti ||
children.translated_text: Then, having mixed cooked rice with sesame flour and ghee, he places the remains of the oblation in the cow-pen on aśvattha leaves, saying, 'To the non-terrible, to the very terrible, homage, homage.'

children.text: athātiśiṣṭaṃ sarvā diśaḥ saṃprakiranti āveśinā vyaśrumukhī kutūhalinyekastanī jṛmbhaṇī stambhanī mohanī ca
children.translated_text: Then they scatter all that is left in every direction, saying, 'The possessing one, the tear-faced one, the curious one, the one-breasted one, the yawning one, the paralyzing one, and the bewildering one,

children.text: kṛṣṇā viśākhā vimalā brahmarātrī bhrātṛvyasaṃkhyeṣu patantyamoghāḥ
children.translated_text: the black one, the branched one, the spotless one, the Brahma-night, the unfailing ones who fall upon countless enemies,

children.text: tābhyo vai mātṛbhyo namo namaḥ iti ||
children.translated_text: to those mothers indeed, homage, homage,' thus.

children.text: sa evameva phalīkaraṇahomaprabhṛti sāyaṃprātar daśarātraṃ karoti ||
children.translated_text: In just this way, beginning with the oblation of parched grain, he performs it evening and morning for ten nights.

children.text: nānutthitāyāṃ sūtikāyāṃ bhojyānnatā ||
children.translated_text: No food fit to be eaten is to be taken while the woman in childbirth has not risen.

children.text: daśamyāmutthānam ||
children.translated_text: The rising takes place on the tenth day.

children.text: daśamyāṃ dvādaśyāṃ vā nāmakaraṇam ||
children.translated_text: The name-giving is on the tenth or the twelfth day.

children.text: prājāpatyena sūktena hutvā brāhmaṇānannena pariviṣya puṇyāhaṃ svasti ṛddhimiti vācayannāmāsmai dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: Having offered with the Prajāpati hymn, having served Brahmins with food, and having them proclaim 'auspicious day, welfare, prosperity,' he gives him a name.

children.text: dvyakṣaraṃ caturakṣaraṃ ṣaḍakṣaramaṣṭākṣaraṃ vā ||
children.translated_text: It should have two syllables, four syllables, six syllables, or eight syllables.

children.text: ghoṣavadādyantarantasthaṃ dīrghābhiniṣṭhānāntam ||
children.translated_text: It should begin with a voiced sound, have a semivowel in the middle or at the end, and end in a long vowel or visarga.

children.text: api vā yasmin svityupasargaḥ syāttaddhi pratiṣṭhitamiti vijñāyate ||
children.translated_text: Or else it may be one in which the prefix su occurs, for that is known to be well established.

children.text: ṛṣyaṇūkaṃ devatāṇūkaṃ vā ||
children.translated_text: It may be modeled on a seer or modeled on a deity.

children.text: yathaivaiṣāṃ pūrvapuruṣāṇāṃ nāmāni syuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Or it may be such as the names of their ancestors were.

children.text: ayugakṣaraṃ kumāryāḥ ||
children.translated_text: For a girl it should have an odd number of syllables.

children.text: amuṣmai svastīti ||
children.translated_text: 'Welfare to this one,' thus.
